title: US bond market closed all day for Columbus Day — with NYSE equities trading a full session
source: NEWS: sifma.org/resources/general/holiday-schedule ('Holiday Schedule', SIFMA's own US Holiday Recommendations panel), fetched direct 2026-09-05 (HTTP 200, 298,899 bytes) and parsed card-by-card out of the page's embedded payload by this session, with region attribution fixed to the page's own 'U.S.' / 'U.K.' / 'Japan' h2 section headings. The US 2026 panel renders holiday/date/note cards in sequence and this one reads exactly 'Columbus Day' / 'Monday, October 12, 2026' with NO 'Early Close' note attached — the full-closure shape, structurally distinct from the early-close cards elsewhere in the same panel (e.g. 'Thanksgiving Day' / 'Thursday, November 26, 2026' / 'Early Close (2:00 p.m. Eastern Time): Friday, November 27, 2026'). Cross-checked the same day against NYSE nyse.com/markets/hours-calendars (HTTP 200 after its 302 to /trade/hours-calendars, 109,180 bytes; its holiday data is '"text":"..."' cells rather than table markup, and all 127 cells were extracted): the grid states 'All NYSE markets observe U.S. holidays as listed below for 2026, 2027, and 2028' and lists nine holidays per year — New Year's Day, MLK Day, Washington's Birthday, Good Friday, Memorial Day, Juneteenth, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving Day, Christmas Day — with ZERO occurrences of the strings 'Columbus', 'Indigenous' or 'October 12' anywhere in the payload, so NYSE equities trade a full 09:30-16:00 ET core session on 2026-10-12 while the recommended USD fixed-income tape is dark. Filed estimate on three counts, identical to sifma-bond-market-closure-2026-11-11 and the three sifma-bond-early-close entries already on this calendar: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no slot for an industry trade association's recommended schedule, this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, and SIFMA's schedule is a recommendation rather than a market-wide halt each firm is bound by. AMENDED 2026-09-05 by this event's own initial research (docs/research/events/sifma-bond-market-closure-2026-10-12.md) with two Federal Reserve primaries the 11-11 sibling did not have, both fetched direct 2026-09-05 and parsed row-by-row: federalreserve.gov/aboutthefed/k8.htm ('K.8 - Holidays Observed by the Federal Reserve System 2026-2030', HTTP 200, 82,205 bytes, page's own 'Last Update: July 8, 2026') and frbservices.org/about/holiday-schedules ('Federal Reserve System Holiday Schedule | Federal Reserve Financial Services', HTTP 200, 94,776 bytes). Both carry the identical row 'Columbus Day | October 12 | October 11 | October 9 | October 8 | October 14' for 2026-2030, so the Federal Reserve Banks observe 2026-10-12 and the FEDERAL-HOLIDAY leg of this entry is now primary-sourced fact rather than inference. The status stays 'estimate' regardless: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts scopes FED: to 'federalreserve.gov FOMC calendar' and has no slot for a holiday schedule, this lane may not self-confirm an in-sweep discovery, and the TRADING claim still rests on SIFMA's non-binding recommendation rather than on either Fed page. Neither Fed payload carries an extractable statement about Fedwire operating hours (the only 'Fedwire' hits in both are navigation menu items, and K.8 defers to the Financial Services holiday page for 'additional details on the operations of the Federal Reserve Banks'), so nothing is asserted here about settlement or payment rails on the closed day.
notes: DISCOVERED during the sifma-bond-market-closure-2026-11-11 initial research (2026-09-05), while testing that entry's own claim to be 'the ONLY full-day cross-asset schedule split in the forward window'. That claim is FALSE and this file is the correction: Columbus Day carries the identical bonds-shut/equities-open shape 30 days EARLIER, on the same SIFMA panel, four cards above the Veterans Day one. The calendar already tracks imf-world-bank-annual-meetings-2026-10-12 on this date but carried nothing about the closure. Why it earns a row rather than a footnote: the 11-11 research measured a real, mechanically-predicted tape signature for this event class — bond ETFs keep trading on NYSE Arca while the cash market they reference is shut, and over 24 Columbus Day sessions (1993-2025, second Monday of October, TLT bars from 2002) TLT traded a median 0.481x its own trailing-20-session median volume with 24 of 24 below 1.0x, LQD 0.395x, against SPY's 0.712x on the same days; the paired TLT-minus-SPY volume-ratio gap is -0.346 (negative in 21 of 24, sign-test p = 0.0001) against an all-Wednesday placebo of +0.039. Columbus Day is in fact the STRONGER of the two samples, so this date is where the 11-11 execution guard was actually validated. STRUCTURAL AND LOW-IMPACT ONLY: a recommended closure moves nothing by itself, no house playbook is calendar- or holiday-keyed (docs/plans/trade-playbooks.md and docs/research/multi-symbol-sweep.md grepped 2026-09-05 for 'holiday|veterans|columbus|closure|half-day|early close' — zero hits in both), and this widens caution about bond-ETF execution depth on 10-12 while licensing nothing. HONEST LIMITS. (1) The kind field: EventKind (src/domain/market-events-types.ts) has no market-structure member, so this is filed 'rates', the same choice sifma-bond-market-closure-2026-11-11 and the sifma-bond-early-close entries already made. (2) The historical sample ASSUMES SIFMA recommended a Columbus Day full closure in every year back to 1993; the published panels cover 2026 and 2027 only, and the archive was not fetched. (3) CME futures hours on 10-12 are NOT asserted: cmegroup.com has returned HTTP 403 to this runner across every prior attempt in sibling lanes. (4) treasurydirect.gov was not fetched, so nothing is asserted about auction or settlement handling on the closed day.
